title: The Guide to Salesforce Agent, Application, and Headless Development
summary: Understand the flexible Salesforce development process, designed to meet the speed and security for any team and project.
body_markdown:
AI’s promise is real, but delivering on it requires more than keeping pace. While business leaders push for the rapid-fire innovation of agents and apps, IT is tasked with turning it into reality — scaling these initiatives without compromising security, compliance, or quality.


The pressure is on, but the development cycles are still riddled with legacy issues: technical debt, unrealistic testing environments, and fragmented governance. These recurring hurdles are holding teams back from meeting the speed and quality expected by this age of AI. It’s time to reimagine development cycles for the agentic era. Teams need a modern, adaptable framework to uphold AI’s promise.


## Many paths to modern development


The landscape of development has fundamentally changed. Today, developers can bring their favorite tools and use open protocols like MCP,[headless development](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/headless-architecture-vs-browser-bound/) lets teams build core logic once and surface rich experiences wherever they need, and intent-based vibe coding paired with enterprise-grade security has made building faster than ever. With so many new pathways emerging, not everyone is taking the same approach.


Teams are making two key choices:


1. How they organize work: solo vs. coordinated
2. How they approach development: human-driven vs. agent-driven


Many teams sit somewhere in between. Where you land on these dimensions shapes what you need from your platform, and that’s exactly what’s driving Salesforce’s evolution.


## A flexible dev process for any team


Get the key steps designed to tackle AI complexity, providing actionable insights and clear guidance for quick and secure innovation.


[Get the guide](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/resources/agent-and-application-development)


## The 6 step process for agent and app development


Salesforce’s approach is designed to be comprehensive, but flexible to custom fit the size and skillset of your team and business priorities. There are six steps:


1. Plan
2. Build
3. Test
4. Deploy
5. Observe
6. Extend


Throughout the entire process, governance is built-in to make sure the most sensitive data stays compliant and secure.


Let’s unpack each of these steps.


### Stage 1. Plan


The planning stage is your opportunity to align everyone involved in development


around common goals and shared expectations. Proper planning can mean avoiding issues down the line, like disconnected development environments or missed deadlines due to poor visibility. In this step, the goal is to ensure that all team members understand project requirements, testing needs, data security standards, and how changes will be managed throughout the project lifecycle.


### Stage 2. Build


Rapid innovation requires a secure environment, also known as a[sandbox](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/sandbox-environments-for-vibe-coding/) . By working in an isolated space, teams do not have to worry about impacting live business operations as they build their solutions.


To build effectively, team members are equipped with their tools of choice. Each type of tool has its own strengths and uses:


- [Vibe coding](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/developers/vibe-coding/) enables anyone to turn ideas into apps, agents, and workflows by simply telling AI what to do.
- Low-code and no-code tools, like[Builder Central](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/builder-central-ai-development/) , helps admins and citizen developers configure apps and agents using visual components.
- Traditional pro-coding isn’t going away — it’s being reallocated. As low code and vibe coding handle the straightforward aspects of a project, coding from scratch shifts toward the elements that need the most customization.


## Build in minutes, not weeks


With Salesforce as your unified development platform, your IT team can quickly build agents and apps with reusable components, pre-built integrations, and low-code tools.


[Download the playbook](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/resources/low-code-playbook/)


### Stage 3. Test


Today’s AI-driven development demands continuous, realistic testing at every step. An environment that mirrors your product setup, like a[Full Copy Sandbox](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/sandboxes-environments/) , ensures that testing is realistic. Effective testing catches issues early, prevents performance bottlenecks, and ensures your agents and apps deliver consistent results every time.


**Pro tip:**[Seed test environments](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/data-masking/) with only the data needed for each scenario. Complement this by masking the data to uphold customer privacy and compliance. This combination speeds up testing and reduces the risk of exposing sensitive info.


### Stage 4. Deploy


No more last-minute scrambles or manual patching. Predictable deployments come from automation, clear visibility, and tight version control. With a streamlined deployment process, teams can avoid business disruptions and human errors. The platform’s built-in[DevOps tools](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/devops-tools/) opens the door for a consistent process. In turn, boosting collaboration, reducing confusion, and helping teams deliver quickly with confidence. Deployment becomes reliable and repeatable — not a high-stakes event.


As users interact with your business across an expanding web of touchpoints, maintaining that reliability requires delivering a consistent experience across every surface. Salesforce’s[Headless Experience Layer](https://www.salesforce.com/headless/orchestration-platform/) separates your business logic, data, and permissions from the screen, so you define your intent once and deploy it wherever your users are.


### Stage 5. Observe


Launching your agent or app doesn’t end there. Once deployed, you’re kicking off a feedback loop. Real success comes from ongoing observability that helps you monitor agent behavior, spot issues early, and optimize over time.


With time, performance evaluations, and user feedback, your solution can always get better over time.


### Stage 6. Extend


Salesforce offers a flexible architecture tailored to your team’s AI maturity, allowing you to integrate preferred third-party developer tools and tap into a rich partner ecosystem.


By leveraging Model Context Protocols (MCPs) across platforms like Slack, Tableau, Informatica, and MuleSoft — alongside Data 360 — teams can ground AI agents in governed enterprise data, analytics, and business logic. Marketplaces like[AppExchange](https://appexchange.salesforce.com/) and[AgentExchange](https://agentexchange.salesforce.com/) further accelerate development by offering ready-to-install apps and agentic components directly within the flow of work. Together, this open ecosystem connects your favorite DevOps and dev tools into a single, unified pipeline from commit to production.


## Governance from the start


Myth: security slows innovation down.


The truth is, security is critical to scale and deploy high quality solutions. Effective governance accelerates innovation because developers aren’t tacking on consistency, compliance, and reliability at the very end of the process. Instead, it’s woven throughout each stage.


## Security is a team effort. We’re with you.


Explore our shared responsibility model and get insights to help you make informed decisions about your security strategy.


[Secure your data](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/resources/foundationals-configurables-enhanceables-guide/)


When you’re thinking about security policies, agent guardrails, and data compliance throughout the process, you’re building a framework that scales with your innovation. When governance is integrated, your team spends less time managing risk.


## The power of the platform


The specific approach you take to these development stages will naturally evolve based on the unique composition and maturity of your team. Different projects require different combinations of these tools and workflows. Ultimately, the Salesforce Platform offers a tech stack that’s built to be modular, allowing you to pick and choose the exact resources you need to bring your specific solution to life efficiently.


If you’d like to dig deeper into each of these steps, check out the[Guide to Agent, App, and Headless Development on Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/platform/resources/agent-and-application-development/) .
